title: Identity building blocks: Azure vs AWS
summary: Both clouds have people, groups, workload identities and permissions, but they're organised differently. Azure keeps every identity in one Entra tenant shared by all subscriptions. AWS keeps identities inside each account and connects accounts through roles.

dimensions.label: Identity directory
values: One Entra tenant, trusted by many subscriptions
IAM per account (Identity Center adds an organisation-wide one)

dimensions.label: People
values: IAM users, or better, Identity Center users

dimensions.label: Groups
values: Entra groups: can be assigned roles directly
IAM groups: only hold policies, can't be a principal

dimensions.label: Workload identity
values: IAM role (instance profile, task role, IRSA…)

dimensions.label: Workload credentials
values: Managed by Azure, or federated credentials
Short-lived STS credentials from assuming a role

dimensions.label: Where permissions are defined
values: Policy attached to the identity, or on the resource

dimensions.label: Default and deny
values: Union of assignments; deny only from managed features
Default deny; an explicit Deny always wins

notes: Azure's 'who can do what where' lives in the role assignment. AWS's lives in policy documents, which can sit on the identity or on the resource itself.
In both, the safest workload identity is one with no stored secret: a managed identity in Azure, a role in AWS.
